annotator_prompt.name: held_color
annotator_prompt.description: After some closed transfers, the release-motion samples already show an empty open hand and do not reveal the released cube's color. The deposited counts alone therefore fail SUFFICIENCY and PREDICTABILITY. Add held_color, with values none, blue, green, or red, initially none. Record the color when a successful grasp is observed; retain it while the cube remains held, including at the closed transfer endpoint before release. Clear it at the first cycle showing the hand empty after release or loss. This field describes observed possession, not an intended grasp or an opening command. For example, write red at a closed transfer endpoint and none at the following completed-release cycle. Existing deposit-count annotations retain their completed-release timing.

policy_prompt_for_memory.name: held_color
policy_prompt_for_memory.description: Sparse release samples can omit the previously held cube, making both its deposit update and the next action unpredictable from counts alone. Initialize held_color to none. Set it to the visibly grasped cube's color when the current views and finger opening establish a successful grasp. Preserve it through closed lifting and transfer, including temporary visual occlusion while possession remains supported. When the hand becomes empty, first use the incoming held_color to evaluate a new release over the bin, then write none. Clear it without counting if the observed loss occurred away from the bin. Do not set it from the cube selected for a future grasp or clear it merely because an opening command is about to be issued. Example: red.

policy_prompt_for_memory.name: deposited_blue
policy_prompt_for_memory.description: When release samples start after separation, the existing requirement for a visible blue carried or falling cube can leave this count unchanged despite an annotated completed release, breaking PREDICTABILITY and sometimes SUFFICIENCY. Keep the existing initialization and evidence rules, but additionally increment once when incoming held_color is blue and the current cycle establishes an empty open hand over the bin following the completed release motion, with no evidence of loss elsewhere. Use incoming held_color before clearing it. Do not require the sampled frames to contain the cube itself. A no-step motion or a hand that was already empty does not qualify. Example: 1. Include only when blue is requested.

policy_prompt_for_memory.name: deposited_green
policy_prompt_for_memory.description: Apply the same sparse-release correction consistently to green: the previous held color can be the only available evidence identifying a newly released cube. Keep existing initialization and release tests, and also increment once when incoming held_color is green and the current cycle establishes an empty open hand over the bin following the completed release motion, with no evidence of loss elsewhere. Evaluate this before clearing held_color. Never count a command about to execute, an already empty hand, or a no-step motion. Example: 2. Include only when green is requested.

policy_prompt_for_memory.name: deposited_red
policy_prompt_for_memory.description: A red release can disappear before the first sampled incoming frame, causing the existing rule to preserve the old count even though the annotated count increases. This breaks PREDICTABILITY. Keep existing initialization and release tests, and additionally increment once when incoming held_color is red and the current cycle establishes an empty open hand over the bin following the completed release motion, with no evidence of loss elsewhere. Evaluate this before clearing held_color; the cube need not appear in the release samples. Never count a future command, an already empty hand, or a no-step motion. Example: 2. Include only when red is requested.

proposal.policy_prompt_for_action:
Sparse release samples sometimes left the hand empty over the bin without identifying the released cube. The policy then failed to update completion and could approach another cube instead of retreating. This is a SUFFICIENCY failure. Extend the effective-count calculation to use the revised memory release test, including incoming held_color, exactly once. An established transition from held cube to empty open hand over the bin requires the usual release retreat even when separation is absent from sampled frames. Compute completion from those effective counts, not from the cleared outgoing held_color.

The mandatory two-camera rim reconstruction repeatedly sent securely held, already lifted cubes upward for visibility recovery when the bin was plainly visible in the front camera but cropped out of the wrist camera. It also blocked release or retreat when the held cube obscured only part of the opening. This breaks SUFFICIENCY. Replace the requirement for cross-camera correspondences with a hierarchy of calibrated geometric methods: use reliable two-view correspondences when available, but accept a single-view reconstruction when the visible bin geometry constrains it. In the single-view case, identify actual table-contact base corners and corresponding vertical wall edges where visible. Intersect base-corner rays with z=0, then fit the corresponding upper corners along world-vertical lines to obtain the rim plane. Back-project inner-rim edge points into that plane and fit the rectangular opening. Use visible opposing edges or reconstruct obscured portions from the fitted rectangle; do not substitute the centroid of an exposed dark fragment. Cross-check the reconstruction against all available visible edges, including partial wrist edges. Do not assume a numerical rim height unsupported by geometry. A cropped wrist image or a partially hidden opening alone is not a reason to recover visibility. Reserve a purposeful viewing motion for genuinely underconstrained geometry.

Use the resulting world opening center consistently for closed transfer and separate release at z=0.20, and for open retreat at [bin_x-0.10, bin_y, 0.20]. Several retreat errors had the correct operation and count but an inaccurate reconstructed center; check opposing edge midlines and reprojection rather than shifting the center toward a visible side wall. Preserve the existing grasp, separate-opening, nonzero-motion, final-retreat, and button-contact rules.
proposal.refused:
The reports correctly identify that choosing any accessible eligible cube does not uniquely reproduce the recorded selections. However, their proposed preferences do not form a consistent rule across the supplied trajectories. Nearest-TCP selection would explain some choices but contradict others where a farther cube of the same eligible color was selected. Fixed left/right preferences and color priorities likewise vary across scenes. One report even calls a target blue although the subsequent grasp and release establish that it was red. No observable universal ranking was established, and adding future target identities to memory would break PREDICTABILITY rather than repair selection. Consequently, do not add per-scene target coordinates, arbitrary left/right priorities, or a universal nearest-cube rule; exact selection remains unresolved by this batch.

The requests to use cube top-face centers rather than whole colored silhouettes are already explicitly covered by the action instruction. The small initial approach and retreat errors that named no missing information do not justify new memory or scene-specific coordinate corrections. The request for a particular perpendicular cube-edge yaw also supplies no general observable convention selecting that branch; both edge alignments are already allowed, and the stated sufficiency test concerns position and gripper state. Do not introduce a yaw history field or hard-coded angle list.

Do not add remembered bin coordinates merely to compensate for wrist cropping: the bin is recoverable from current scene geometry, so such a field has not met NECESSITY. Also do not invent a fixed numerical rim height from the suggested single-view fallback; use observable geometry as specified instead.

Evaluate that test before clearing held_color, and compute completion from the resulting per-color counts, not from outgoing held_color. Multiple evidence tests for one release still produce only one increment.

policy_prompt_for_action.modify_from: Reconstruct the bin's rectangular inner opening from calibrated current front and wrist views. Identify corresponding inner-rim corners or edge intersections. For each image point [u,v,1], form a world ray with camera center C=-R^T t and direction d=R^T K^-1[u,v,1], using that camera's current calibration. Triangulate reliable corresponding rim points and fit their common horizontal plane. Fit the rectangular inner opening to visible opposing edges in that plane; reconstruct occluded corners from the fitted edges rather than using the centroid of the visible dark fragment. Compute the world center from opposing corners or edge midlines, and check that the fitted opening reprojects onto visible rim segments in both views. Do not average image centroids across cameras, use occluding silhouette boundaries as rim correspondences, or intersect the opening center with the tabletop. If reliable reconstruction is unavailable, use the purposeful visibility-recovery motion below rather than inventing a rim height.
policy_prompt_for_action.modify_to: Reconstruct the bin's rectangular inner opening using the available calibrated current views. For each image point [u,v,1], form a world ray with camera center C=-R^T t and direction d=R^T K^-1[u,v,1], using that camera's current calibration. Prefer reliable two-view correspondences between actual inner-rim corners or edge intersections: triangulate them and fit their common horizontal plane. When such correspondences are unavailable, accept a single-view reconstruction if visible geometry constrains it. Identify actual table-contact base corners and their corresponding vertical wall edges; intersect base-corner rays with z=0, then fit corresponding upper corners along the world-vertical lines through those base corners to determine the rim plane. Back-project inner-rim edge points into that plane and fit the rectangular opening. Use visible opposing edges and reconstruct obscured portions only where the fitted geometry constrains them. Compute the world center from opposing corners or edge midlines, and verify reprojection against all available visible rim segments, including partial wrist edges. Do not shift the center toward a visible side wall, use the centroid of an exposed dark fragment, average image centroids across cameras, treat occluding silhouettes as rim correspondences, or intersect the opening center with the tabletop. A cropped wrist view or partial opening occlusion alone does not require visibility recovery. Use the purposeful visibility-recovery motion below only when the available geometry is genuinely underconstrained; do not invent a numeric rim height.

policy_prompt_for_action.modify_from: When the hand is empty and open at the bin after a release, retreat toward the robot: target [bin_x-0.10, bin_y, 0.20], preserving orientation and keeping open.
policy_prompt_for_action.modify_to: When the hand is empty and open at the bin after a release, including a release established using incoming held_color without a sampled separation, retreat toward the robot: target [bin_x-0.10, bin_y, 0.20], preserving orientation and keeping open.

policy_prompt_for_action.modify_from: If an object needed for localization is occluded, move upward to a clear viewing height while retaining any held cube, then re-localize.
policy_prompt_for_action.modify_to: If occlusion leaves an object needed for localization genuinely underconstrained after using the available calibrated views and visible geometry, move upward to a clear viewing height while retaining any held cube, then re-localize. No fixed color priority, nearest-cube ranking, left/right preference, future target list, or scene-specific coordinates are added; all three rounds leave exact new-target selection unresolved. fields.name: deposited_blue
fields.description: Include only when blue is requested. Initialize to 0 when memory is empty; otherwise carry forward. Increment once when this cycle's incoming motion shows either a blue cube carried over the bin followed by an empty open hand, or a blue cube separating or falling directly below the fingers over the opening followed by an empty open hand. The sampled frames need not show the finger-opening transition itself. Require evidence of a new release from this hand over the bin; a stationary tabletop cube below the hand or an unrelated falling cube is not release evidence. Identify color from the carried or newly released cube, not remaining tabletop objects. Alternatively, when incoming held_color is blue, count a newly established transition to an empty open hand over the bin in the executed incoming release motion, with no evidence of loss elsewhere, even if all sampled frames omit the cube. Use incoming held_color before clearing it. This is an alternative evidence test for the same release, not an additional increment; an already empty hand or a no-step motion does not qualify. Count even if the resting cube is hidden and even if the motion includes retreat. Never increment for the command about to be issued, an already empty hand, a grasp, a closed transfer, retreat without a new release, or a motion executing no steps. Preserve through button pressing. e.g. 2

Do not increment when merely choosing the opening command, for grasps or closed transfers, or for later views of a completed release. Preserve otherwise, including through button pressing. e.g. 2

texts.action:
Read a separate quota for each requested color from the goal each cycle. For each color, compute its completed count from its incoming deposited_<color> memory plus only that color's newly completed release in the current incoming motion, exactly once, using the memory instruction's sparse-frame evidence test. A carried cube followed by an empty open hand, or a cube visibly separating or falling from the fingers over the opening followed by an empty open hand, can establish the release without a sampled finger-opening transition. Also apply the memory instruction's incoming-held_color test when the released cube is absent from all incoming samples. Evaluate that test before clearing held_color, and compute completion from the resulting per-color counts, not from outgoing held_color. Multiple evidence tests for one release still produce only one increment. Do not add the release again to an already updated count. A color is eligible only while its own quota remains outstanding. Completion requires every requested color's quota to be satisfied. Start with an open hand and zero deposits for each requested color. Infer object positions from calibrated front and wrist views rather than treating image coordinates as world coordinates. Cubes are approximately 4 cm wide: identify and back-project their top-face centers at approximately z=0.04 and use the resulting world xy for approach and the z=0.02 grasp. Use the top face, not the whole visible silhouette; visible side faces must not bias the center. Reconstruct the bin's rectangular inner opening using the available calibrated current views. For each image point [u,v,1], form a world ray with camera center C=-R^T t and direction d=R^T K^-1[u,v,1], using that camera's current calibration. Prefer reliable two-view correspondences between actual inner-rim corners or edge intersections: triangulate them and fit their common horizontal plane. When such correspondences are unavailable, accept a single-view reconstruction if visible geometry constrains it. Identify actual table-contact base corners and their corresponding vertical wall edges; intersect base-corner rays with z=0, then fit corresponding upper corners along the world-vertical lines through those base corners to determine the rim plane. Back-project inner-rim edge points into that plane and fit the rectangular opening. Use visible opposing edges and reconstruct obscured portions only where the fitted geometry constrains them. Compute the world center from opposing corners or edge midlines, and verify reprojection against all available visible rim segments, including partial wrist edges. Do not shift the center toward a visible side wall, use the centroid of an exposed dark fragment, average image centroids across cameras, treat occluding silhouettes as rim correspondences, or intersect the opening center with the tabletop. A cropped wrist view or partial opening occlusion alone does not require visibility recovery. Use the purposeful visibility-recovery motion below only when the available geometry is genuinely underconstrained; do not invent a numeric rim height. Use this same geometrically defined center for closed transfer and separate release at z=0.20 and for retreat at [bin_x-0.10,bin_y,0.20]. Locate the button by its gray circular top on a light square base; back-project the top center at approximately z=0.02 and use that xy for approach and press. Re-estimate positions from current views; scene objects can appear during execution. Robot right is negative world y.

When any color quota remains outstanding and the hand is empty away from the bin's release position, select a visible, accessible tabletop cube of an eligible color. Prefer a clear grasp and maintain the selection when the hand is already aligned above an eligible cube; do not switch cubes or colors simply because new cubes appear. Never select another cube of a color whose quota is already satisfied. Approach its center at z=0.15 with the gripper open, roll=-3.1416, pitch=0, and a feasible yaw aligned with a cube edge. Do not constrain yaw to [-0.7854,0.7854]. Re-estimate edge alignment for each newly selected cube rather than carrying over the previous cube's yaw, and preserve the selected orientation through descent and lift. When already above an eligible cube near z=0.15, identify the approached cube by projecting [current_tcp_x,current_tcp_y,0.04] into the current wrist image with its calibration. Identify the eligible top face nearest that projection, cross-checking world-space proximity and the incoming approach frames. Neither the wrist image center nor the largest visible cube is the alignment reference. Refine that same cube's top-face center at approximately z=0.04, then descend at its world xy to z=0.02 and close, preserving the approached cube's edge-aligned orientation. Do not switch to another prominent cube or descend at an inaccurate measured approach xy.

When a cube is grasped at table height, lift vertically to z=0.15, retaining its grasp orientation and keeping the gripper closed. A cube between the fingers and finger positions around 0.018 m support a successful grasp. Once lifted, move to the visually localized world xy center of the bin opening at z=0.20, keeping the cube closed in the gripper and preserving the measured grasp orientation. After the closed-hand transfer reaches approximately z=0.20 above the bin, re-localize the opening and command open at [bin_x, bin_y, 0.20], correcting any residual lateral error in that waypoint. The target is the opening center, not the measured TCP xy. Opening remains a separate operation from the closed-hand transfer. Correct both lateral coordinates before testing whether the centered target would produce no motion; add a 0.003 m vertical displacement only in that case.

When the hand is empty and open at the bin after a release, including a release established using incoming held_color without a sampled separation, retreat toward the robot: target [bin_x-0.10, bin_y, 0.20], preserving orientation and keeping open. Compute this offset from the visually localized bin center, never from measured TCP xy. Perform this retreat even after the final requested cube. If the incoming motion already included this retreat and the hand is at that offset, do not repeat it. Retreat clears the opening and gives the dropped cube time to fall; no separate arbitrary wait is needed.

When every requested color's quota is satisfied and the final release retreat is finished, ignore all remaining cubes. Approach the button center at z=0.15, roll=-3.1416, pitch=0, yaw=0, with the gripper open. When already aligned above the button with open fingers, re-localize the gray circular button-top center, back-projecting it at approximately z=0.02 and checking the other current view when visible. Use the circular top, not the surrounding square base. Command [button_x,button_y,0.15,-3.1416,0,0] and close the empty gripper. Correct the target before testing the nonzero-motion requirement; add a 0.003 m vertical displacement only if the corrected target would otherwise produce no motion. When aligned above the button with closed fingers, descend to [button_x, button_y, 0.0075] with the gripper closed. If the current motion shows this descent reaching button contact, retract to [button_x, button_y, 0.15] with the gripper still closed. Contact can leave the measured TCP near z=0.0245 rather than the commanded depth; recognize the visible contact and retract instead of repeatedly demanding a deeper press.

For an unanticipated or ambiguous situation, use the visible hand contents, finger opening, height, and object alignment to recover the applicable rule. Never increase the deposit count without an observed release. If a grasp fails, reopen with a small nonzero upward motion and re-approach a visible requested-color cube. If any color quota remains outstanding but no suitable cube of an eligible color is currently available, wait 16 control steps specifically to observe newly arriving cubes, then reassess. If occlusion leaves an object needed for localization genuinely underconstrained after using the available calibrated views and visible geometry, move upward to a clear viewing height while retaining any held cube, then re-localize. Do not make this recovery motion merely because the wrist view crops the object or part of it is hidden. Never press the stop button before every requested color's quota is satisfied and the final release retreat is complete.
